_comment: SPARK — S165 P3: atlas specs for the six TIER-3 TOWER units (R116/R134).
⭐ ticksPerFrame MATCHES THE SHIPPED ROSTER — idle 7, walk 4, attack 5, die 5 — so a tier-3 unit
animates at the same cadence as every other creature on the board rather than reading as a
separate game.
⭐ cellH IS UNIFORM AT 200 ACROSS ALL SIX, AND THAT IS A CONTRACT, NOT A CONVENIENCE.
build-sprite-atlas.mjs HEIGHT-FITS (`scale = cellH / bboxH`), and each race is its own atlas, so
the union-bbox anti-jitter guarantee does not span them. If one race's cellH differed, that race's
unit would silently render at a different size from its siblings and nothing would catch it.
src/render/raceUnitFrames.test.ts pins exactly this invariant for the castle six.
⚠ SO HOW DO A BAT AND AN ORC RAIDER END UP DIFFERENT SIZES ON THE BOARD? Not here. A uniform
cellH means every unit is drawn at the same CELL height; any per-creature size differentiation is
a RENDER-TIME scale constant, which is how the shipped goblin roster already does it. That
constant is deliberately NOT written yet: R135 gives these six varied stats and supplies no
figures, so a size ladder invented here would be MINE and would have to be redone the moment the
owner rules. Art first, numbers when they exist.
⚠ cellW is a FLOOR, not a cap — the builder widens the cell to fit the subject. The bat's
wingspan, the piranha's leap arc and the wraith's trailing smoke will each push theirs wider, the
way the naga's tail did. Width varies legitimately; height must not.
⛔ `die` IS BUILT AND NOTHING PLAYS IT, same as the castle six. goblinRenderer maps three FSM
states and creatures are removed the instant they are killed, so there is no window a death row
could be seen in. The builder is generic over the states dict so the row costs nothing to bake; it
ships ready and the sim-side dying window is its own piece of work.
⛔ enclosedWhiteLimitPct 4e-05 ON ALL SIX, with no per-character exception. The castle six needed
an orc-specific 0.0003 override because that character's eyes and the background leaks measured
the SAME SIZE and no size rule could separate them. These six were generated under the S165
colour-cast clause — every pale area is a NAMED tinted colour, never a near-white — so by
construction every near-white pocket in the frame is background and the aggressive limit is safe.
⚠ VERIFY THAT ON THE BUILT SHEETS rather than trusting it: if a bone-yellow tusk or a magenta eye
comes out desaturated enough to trip `max-min < 28`, it will be punched out.
